title: Enterprise Recoverability, Ransomware Resilience and DR Assurance Capstone
summary: Integrate recovery objectives, immutable protection, dependency mapping, restore evidence and controlled failover/failback into an enterprise recoverability assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit a business-critical estate with nominally successful backups but inconsistent restore testing, dependency maps and ransomware recovery evidence. Leadership requires an evidence-backed recoverability decision before the next resilience review.
business_context: Recovery success is measured by restored business service within approved RPO/RTO, not by backup-job completion alone.
technical_constraints: Assessment starts read-only. Retention changes, recovery-point deletion, production restore, failover/failback, key changes and destructive cleanup require separate approved authority.
functional_requirements: Map service RPO/RTO, recovery tier, owner and critical dependencies.
Reconcile protected scope, recovery points, retention/immutability and key-access assumptions.
Assess ransomware separation between production and backup administration.
Review restore-test evidence against data consistency, dependency readiness and elapsed recovery time.
Build a controlled DR sequence covering declaration, failover, validation, communications and failback.
Produce prioritized recoverability gaps with owner, risk, validation and escalation boundary.
non_functional_requirements: No recovery data or retention policy is mutated during evidence collection.
A green backup dashboard is never treated as proof of recoverability.
Recommendations preserve evidence and define approval/rollback boundaries.
implementation_plan: Map dependencies and administrative compromise paths.
Produce an executive recoverability decision and remediation backlog.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend whether the service is recoverable within RPO/RTO using traceable protection, dependency, restore-test and DR evidence.
rollback_dr: Any later restore, failover, failback, retention or key change remains separately authorized with explicit data-protection and rollback boundaries.

assessment_rubric.recovery_objectives: Connects business RPO/RTO to technical evidence.
assessment_rubric.recoverability_evidence: Distinguishes job success from tested restore assurance.
assessment_rubric.ransomware_resilience: Evaluates administrative separation, immutability and key dependencies.
assessment_rubric.dr_judgement: Defines controlled failover, validation and failback boundaries.

title: vSphere Cluster Resilience, Mobility and Lifecycle Assurance Capstone
summary: Integrate vCenter/ESXi boundaries, HA, DRS, vMotion, storage/network dependencies and lifecycle evidence into a production vSphere assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit a production vSphere cluster approaching lifecycle maintenance. Cluster dashboards are mostly healthy, but evacuation headroom, DRS constraints, network/storage dependencies and post-remediation acceptance evidence are incomplete.
business_context: Maintenance must preserve workload availability and avoid turning lifecycle work into a capacity, migration, network or storage incident.
technical_constraints: Discovery is read-only. Maintenance mode, vMotion, HA/DRS policy changes, lifecycle remediation, distributed-switch/storage changes and host reboot require approved change authority.
functional_requirements: Separate vCenter control-plane state from ESXi and workload health.
Map HA/DRS configuration, admission constraints, VM/Host rules and evacuation headroom.
Reconcile vMotion, management, workload network and datastore dependencies.
Review desired lifecycle state and compatibility evidence without remediation.
Build an incident flow for migration, maintenance or remediation failure.
Define measurable pre/post maintenance acceptance and rollback criteria.
non_functional_requirements: Cluster visual balance is not treated as proof of DRS correctness or failure.
Post-change acceptance includes workload-level evidence, not only completed tasks.
implementation_plan: Baseline vCenter, cluster and host state.
Assess placement rules, capacity and mobility dependencies.
Produce a prioritized readiness and remediation backlog.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend a lifecycle go/no-go decision using control-plane, cluster, capacity, network, storage and workload evidence.
rollback_dr: Any later remediation or migration requires approved rollback, workload recovery and post-change validation boundaries.

assessment_rubric.layered_reasoning: Separates vCenter, host, cluster and workload failure domains.
assessment_rubric.mobility_readiness: Validates compatibility, rules, capacity, network and storage before migration.
assessment_rubric.lifecycle_safety: Defines staged remediation and measurable acceptance criteria.
assessment_rubric.operational_judgement: Avoids forced change before constraints and rollback are understood.

title: Cloud Cost Accountability, Optimization and Unit-Economics Capstone
summary: Integrate allocation, anomaly analysis, optimization, commitment governance and business-value evidence into a multi-cloud FinOps decision exercise.
scenario: Cloud spend has risen materially while allocation quality, shared-cost rules and optimization recommendations are disputed. Leadership wants savings, but no production-risk or long-term commitment decision may be made from a dashboard recommendation alone.
business_context: The objective is accountable business value per unit of technology consumption, not indiscriminate cost reduction.
technical_constraints: Analysis is read-only. Resource deletion/stopping, scaling changes, budget changes and financial commitments require separate technical and financial approval.
functional_requirements: Normalize billing scope, period, currency and allocation dimensions.
Quantify unattributed/shared spend and document ownership rules.
Decompose material variance into usage, deployment, allocation and rate effects.
Evaluate rightsizing and commitment recommendations against demand history and architecture constraints.
Define unit-economics measures tied to meaningful business outcomes.
Produce a prioritized optimization portfolio with savings hypothesis, reliability risk, owner and approval boundary.
non_functional_requirements: No destructive optimization is performed during analysis.
Savings claims distinguish forecast from realized evidence.
Reliability, performance, licensing and commitment risks remain explicit.
implementation_plan: Define unit-economics measures and decision owners.
validation: Passes when the learner can explain cost variance, allocation confidence, optimization trade-offs and business-value impact without treating lower spend as the sole success criterion.
rollback_dr: Any production optimization or financial commitment remains a separately approved decision with technical rollback or commercial exit assumptions documented.

assessment_rubric.allocation_quality: Makes ownership and shared-cost rules auditable.
assessment_rubric.variance_reasoning: Separates usage, allocation, deployment and rate effects.
assessment_rubric.optimization_judgement: Balances savings with architecture and commitment risk.
assessment_rubric.business_value: Uses meaningful unit economics rather than absolute spend alone.

title: Service Reliability Architecture, SLO and Incident-Learning Capstone
summary: Integrate SLO design, observability, dependency analysis, resilience trade-offs and incident learning into an end-to-end service reliability review.
scenario: A business-critical service reports acceptable component uptime but recurring customer-visible degradation. Monitoring is noisy, dependency ownership is incomplete and recent incidents have not produced durable architecture improvements.
business_context: Reliability must be measured at meaningful user journeys and balanced transparently against delivery velocity, cost and operational complexity.
technical_constraints: Review begins read-only. SLO changes, alert changes, scaling, routing, failover and topology mutation require approved service/change authority.
functional_requirements: Identify critical user journeys and define defensible SLIs/SLOs.
Map dependencies, failure domains, capacity assumptions and recovery paths.
Assess telemetry coverage across latency, traffic, errors and saturation.
Correlate incidents with deployments, configuration changes and dependency events.
Evaluate resilience proposals for shared dependencies, operational complexity and cost trade-offs.
Produce owned architecture/reliability actions with measurable verification criteria.
non_functional_requirements: Component uptime alone is not accepted as service reliability evidence.
Alerts require ownership and actionable response expectations.
Incident learning addresses systemic contributing conditions rather than individual blame.
implementation_plan: Baseline user journeys and service objectives.
Produce prioritized architecture decisions and corrective actions.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend service objectives, explain observed reliability gaps and propose bounded improvements with measurable evidence and trade-offs.
rollback_dr: Any later topology, scaling, failover, monitoring or SLO mutation remains separately approved with rollback and post-change service validation.

assessment_rubric.service_objectives: Defines user-visible SLIs/SLOs with clear ownership.
assessment_rubric.observability: Uses complementary telemetry and actionable alert reasoning.
assessment_rubric.resilience: Identifies shared failure domains and recovery assumptions.
assessment_rubric.incident_learning: Turns evidence into durable, owned architecture improvements.
